cases.name: PGP1 / PGPS1
cases.quote: In this study, we characterized the photosynthesis of an Arabidopsis thaliana T-DNA insertional mutant (pgp1-2), which lacks plastidic PG biosynthesis.
cases.review: The article names the Arabidopsis PGP1 knockout and directly studies the loss of plastidic phosphatidylglycerol biosynthesis and its photosynthetic consequences. This supports the chosen biological-process answer. It is mutant-phenotype support, not a new purified-enzyme assay of every reaction detail stated in the generated explanation.
cases.limitation: The teacher explanation adds the enzyme reaction. This specific paper supports the biological process and mutant phenotype; it does not independently verify each enzyme-reaction detail or establish that the answer can be inferred from sequence alone.

cases.generated_training_explanation: The protein catalyzes transfer of a phosphatidyl group from CDP-diacylglycerol to glycerol-3-phosphate, producing phosphatidylglycerophosphate, an intermediate in phosphatidylglycerol synthesis. The sequence alone does not establish that function.

cases.name: VCCN2 / BEST2
cases.section: Results → AtVCCNs are thylakoid members of a conserved channel family; Figure 1
cases.quote: Immunoblotting of chloroplast subfractions isolated from leaves of transformed plants revealed a location for both AtVCCNs in the thylakoid membrane
cases.review: The paper identifies At2g45870 as AtVCCN2 and distinguishes it from the close paralogue AtVCCN1. It reports chloroplast colocalization and thylakoid-fraction immunoblots for both proteins. Those results support the selected thylakoid-membrane location for this exact protein.
cases.limitation: O80832 is VCCN2, not VCCN1. The paper focuses its physiological and electrophysiological characterization on VCCN1; the demonstrated VCCN2 localization should not be treated as proof of every VCCN1 functional claim. The training question and rationale include a chloride-channel/PMF premise; the narrower localization answer is what this example verifies.

cases.name: TCL2
cases.section: Results → TCL2 interacts with GL3; Figure 6A
cases.quote: indicating that TCL2 interacts with GL3 in plant cells
cases.review: The article identifies Arabidopsis At2g30424 as TCL2 and reports a cell-based protein-interaction assay with controls. Its Results and Figure 6A support interaction with GL3, which is exactly the selected answer.
cases.limitation: The paper supports the stated interaction under the reported experimental conditions. It does not make GL3 inferable from the letters of the sequence alone or establish that GL3 is the only possible interaction partner.
